archive.path_sha256_basis: Recomputed from the blobs committed at 990fc0686 with `git show <sha>:<path>`, never copied from the receipt's self-report. The receipt's own entry reads SELF there because a receipt cannot hash its own final bytes; this block closes it. One path was REMOVED from this block after the dispatcher rejected it: see undeclared_artifact_not_bound_by_this_archive. The snapshot receipt committed at 990fc0686 still lists it, so the receipt binds 8 paths and this authoritative block binds the 7 declared ones; the difference is exactly that undeclared seal and is deliberate.

undeclared_artifact_not_bound_by_this_ar.why_it_is_not_bound: It is NOT in TASK-20260903-9318b5's declared artifact_paths, whose sole deliverable is verdict-tables-005.yaml. The dispatcher refused the archive for binding a path outside the union of the archive's and its sources' declared artifact_paths, and that refusal is CORRECT. The seal exists because the orchestrating session's task card asked the reader to hash its verdicts before opening the anchors, not because the committed contract required it.
undeclared_artifact_not_bound_by_this_ar.why_the_contract_was_not_amended_to_fit_: Widening a completed task's artifact_paths after the fact so that an artifact produced outside the contract validates against it is retroactive fitting -- the same failure mode this batch exists to measure. The gap is recorded instead.
undeclared_artifact_not_bound_by_this_ar.what_is_lost_and_what_is_not: LOST: this archive gives the seal no content binding. NOT LOST: the seal is pinned in git at 74eec580b, committed in flight BEFORE the task returned, and the orchestrating session verified after the return that the worktree copy is byte-identical to that commit -- so the seal was not rewritten to match the outcome. That check is what makes the -005 column's blindness claim auditable at all.
undeclared_artifact_not_bound_by_this_ar.owed_at_batch_close: DEC-20260903-9c3e26 should rule on whether a review task whose protocol requires a pre-read seal must declare that seal in artifact_paths. As written, the batch's most load-bearing integrity artifact is the one the formal archive cannot cover.

superseded_archive_commit.why: Its message omitted RQ-AES-002, which content_first requires, and it was already pushed. Superseded forward rather than amended: rewriting history over pushed archive records is what CORR-20260802-a1f151 records five goals losing. The commit remains in history and is not rewritten.

receipt_parent_sha_correction.cause: b70aae863 is the parent of the SUPERSEDED archive commit 990fc0686. When the archive was re-committed as 4f5115ad0 to carry binding_mode content_first and the RQ-AES-002 id, the orchestrating session updated this queue block and did NOT update the same field inside the receipt. The receipt therefore names the parent of a commit it is no longer part of.
receipt_parent_sha_correction.severity: Advisory under content_first, and the dispatcher verified the correct value from THIS block, so the archive verification is sound and is not being re-asserted on weaker evidence. It is still a wrong binding field in an archive receipt -- the failure class CORR-20260802-a1f151 records five goals losing -- so it is corrected here rather than left for a later reader.
receipt_parent_sha_correction.why_the_receipt_is_not_edited: The receipt is committed and hash-bound at 4f5115ad0. Editing it would change its digest, invalidate the binding this block just established, and require a third archive commit. Records are corrected by superseding, never by overwriting; this block is the superseding record and the authoritative value.
receipt_parent_sha_correction.owed_at_batch_close: DEC-20260903-9c3e26 should note that a receipt's own commit_binding can go stale on supersession while the queue stays right, and that only the queue block is authoritative.
